questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Complete a precise definition. A counterclockwise rotation about point O through angle θ maps each point P ≠ O to the point P′ such that ______ and ______. Point O maps to ______.
questions.prompt_markup: Complete a precise definition. A counterclockwise rotation about point O through angle θ maps each point P ≠ O to the point P′ such that ______ and ______. Point O maps to ______.
questions.correct_answer: OP′ = OP (P′ is on the circle with center O through P); m∠POP′ = θ, measured counterclockwise from ray OP; itself.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent wording. All three blanks are needed.

questions.prompt: A rotation maps P(2, 0) to P′(0, 2). Explain why its center must lie on the line y = x.

sections.skill: Find the center and angle of a rotation from points and their images

branch.new_demand: Solve the inverse problem: find the center and angle of a rotation from points and their images.
branch.builds_on: FORWARD 1 rotates about any given center; FORWARD 2 reverses the task and finds the center and angle.

questions.skill: Find the center and angle of a rotation from points and their images
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A rotation maps B(1, 0) to B′(0, 1) and A(3, 1) to A′(-1, 3). The center is where the perpendicular bisectors of BB′ and AA′ meet. Find the center and the angle of rotation.
questions.prompt_markup: A rotation maps B(1, 0) to B′(0, 1) and A(3, 1) to A′(-1, 3). The center is where the perpendicular bisectors of BB′ and AA′ meet. Find the center and the angle of rotation.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the center and the angle with direction. The bisector of BB′ is y = x; the bisector of AA′ passes through (1, 2) with slope 2, which is y = 2x. They meet at (0, 0), and (1, 0) → (0, 1) is a 90° counterclockwise turn.
